```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(framework)
scaffold()
```

This project has three connections in `settings/connections.yml`:

- `study`: the shared study database at `../../shared/study.sqlite`, which
  the R, Python, and Stata projects all use. It has `read_only: true`, so
  Framework opens it read-only.
- `analysis`: a local SQLite file (`analysis.sqlite`, gitignored) for the
  write demos.
- `framework`: Framework's own `framework.db`, which holds the catalog,
  results, and cache records.

## What's configured

`connections_list()` shows database and object storage connections;
`db_list()` shows databases only. SQLite paths are relative to the project
root, not to `notebooks/`.

```{r}
connections_list()
```

```{r}
db_list()
```

`db_drivers_status()` reports which DBI driver packages are installed, and
`db_drivers_install()` installs missing ones.

```{r}
db_drivers_status()
```

## Querying the study database

`db_query()` opens the connection, runs the query, and closes it. This counts
enrolment by site and arm. Look for a roughly even split within each site.

```{r}
db_query(
  "SELECT s.site_name, s.setting, p.treatment, COUNT(*) AS n
   FROM participants p
   JOIN sites s ON s.site_id = p.site_id
   GROUP BY s.site_name, s.setting, p.treatment
   ORDER BY s.site_name, p.treatment",
  "study"
)
```

Extra arguments go to `DBI::dbGetQuery()`, so parameterized queries work.
This pulls the intervention arm's visits for participants 60 and older.

```{r}
older_intervention <- db_query(
  "SELECT v.participant_id, v.visit_number, v.systolic_bp
   FROM visits v
   JOIN participants p ON p.participant_id = v.participant_id
   WHERE p.treatment = ? AND p.age >= ?",
  "study",
  params = list("intervention", 60)
)
nrow(older_intervention)
head(older_intervention)
```

Views work like tables. `participant_summary` has one row per participant.

```{r}
db_query("SELECT * FROM participant_summary LIMIT 5", "study")
```

## Several queries on one connection

`db_with()` opens one connection, makes it available as `conn` inside the
block, and closes it afterwards, even on error. Use it when you need more
than one query.

```{r}
mean_sbp_by_visit <- db_with("study", {
  tables <- DBI::dbListTables(conn)
  message("Tables: ", paste(tables, collapse = ", "))

  DBI::dbGetQuery(conn, "
    SELECT p.treatment, v.visit_number,
           COUNT(v.systolic_bp) AS n,
           ROUND(AVG(v.systolic_bp), 1) AS mean_systolic
    FROM visits v
    JOIN participants p ON p.participant_id = v.participant_id
    GROUP BY p.treatment, v.visit_number
    ORDER BY p.treatment, v.visit_number")
})
mean_sbp_by_visit
```

Fewer participants have visits 3 and 4, so later means rest on smaller groups.

## Managing a connection yourself

`db_connect()` returns a DBI connection that you close yourself. Use it for
interactive work with DBI or dbplyr.

```{r}
conn <- db_connect("study")
DBI::dbListFields(conn, "survey")
DBI::dbGetQuery(conn, "SELECT satisfaction, COUNT(*) AS n FROM survey GROUP BY satisfaction")
DBI::dbDisconnect(conn)
```

## The study connection is read-only

`read_only: true` in the connection's settings opens the SQLite file
read-only. It works even on a file you don't have write permission for.

```{r}
settings("connections.databases.study")
```

`db_execute()` refuses a read-only connection before it touches the database.
Look for "is read-only".

```{r}
#| error: true
db_execute("DELETE FROM visits WHERE systolic_bp IS NULL", "study")
```

`db_transaction()` refuses it too.

```{r}
#| error: true
db_with("study", {
  db_transaction(conn, {
    DBI::dbExecute(conn, "UPDATE participants SET bmi = NULL")
  })
})
```

Even raw DBI calls on the connection fail, because SQLite itself opened the
file read-only.

```{r}
#| error: true
db_with("study", DBI::dbExecute(conn, "DROP VIEW participant_summary"))
```

Reads are unaffected.

```{r}
db_query("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_visits FROM visits", "study")
```

## Writing to the local database

The write demos use the `analysis` connection. `db_execute()` runs a statement
and returns the number of rows affected.

```{r}
db_execute("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS site_bp", "analysis")
db_execute(
  "CREATE TABLE site_bp (
     site_name TEXT,
     treatment TEXT,
     n INTEGER,
     mean_systolic REAL,
     PRIMARY KEY (site_name, treatment)
   )",
  "analysis"
)
```

Summaries computed from the study database are written into the local one.

```{r}
site_bp <- db_query(
  "SELECT site_name, treatment, COUNT(*) AS n, ROUND(AVG(mean_systolic_bp), 1) AS mean_systolic
   FROM participant_summary GROUP BY site_name, treatment",
  "study"
)

db_with("analysis", {
  DBI::dbAppendTable(conn, "site_bp", site_bp)
})
db_query("SELECT * FROM site_bp", "analysis")
```

`db_execute()` also takes `params`.

```{r}
db_execute(
  "UPDATE site_bp SET mean_systolic = ROUND(mean_systolic, 0) WHERE treatment = ?",
  "analysis",
  params = list("control")
)
```

## Transactions

`db_transaction()` runs a block on a connection and commits only if every
statement succeeds. This one adds a flag column and fills it in.

```{r}
db_with("analysis", {
  db_transaction(conn, {
    DBI::dbExecute(conn, "ALTER TABLE site_bp ADD COLUMN above_130 INTEGER")
    DBI::dbExecute(conn, "UPDATE site_bp SET above_130 = mean_systolic >= 130")
  })
})
db_query("SELECT * FROM site_bp ORDER BY mean_systolic DESC", "analysis")
```

The second transaction deletes the control rows and then hits a duplicate key.
The error rolls the whole block back, so the row count stays at 8. Look for
"Transaction failed and was rolled back".

```{r}
#| error: true
db_with("analysis", {
  db_transaction(conn, {
    DBI::dbExecute(conn, "DELETE FROM site_bp WHERE treatment = 'control'")
    DBI::dbExecute(conn, "INSERT INTO site_bp (site_name, treatment) VALUES ('North Clinic', 'intervention')")
  })
})
```

```{r}
db_query("SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_after_rollback FROM site_bp", "analysis")
```

## Inside framework.db

The `framework` connection is Framework's own bookkeeping. You can read it like
any database: the `data` table holds the catalog hashes from notebook 02.

```{r}
db_query("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' ORDER BY name", "framework")
db_query("SELECT name, type, locked, substr(hash, 1, 12) AS hash FROM data", "framework")
```
